hints: Look backwards from the product, the target has a ketone at C3 and a carboxylic acid at C1, so think what functional groups can be oxidised to these.
Remember that a secondary alcohol oxidises to a ketone, a primary alcohol or aldehyde oxidises to a carboxylic acid, and a halogenoalkane hydrolyses to an alcohol.
Check if each of 1, 2 and 3 can reach a hydroxy intermediate in one step, then be oxidised to the keto-acid in the second step.
walkthrough:
**Identify the target functional groups**

Look closely at 3-oxobutanoic acid. It is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{COOH}$, a 4-carbon chain with a ketone on C3 and a carboxylic acid on C1.

This combination screams oxidation products:

**Recall the key oxidation and substitution routes**

Remember these core AS reactions in simple terms.

$$\text{secondary alcohol} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{ketone}$$
$$\text{primary alcohol / aldehyde} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{carboxylic acid}$$
$$\text{R-X} \xrightarrow{\text{NaOH(aq), heat}} \text{R-OH}$$
$$\text{alkene} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4 \text{ then H}_2\text{O}} \text{alcohol (Markovnikov)}$$

**Test structure 2 and structure 3**

Structure 2 is $\text{CH}_3\text{CHClCH}_2\text{COOH}$. Hydrolyse the C-Cl to C-OH with aqueous NaOH to give $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{COOH}$, then oxidise the secondary alcohol to the ketone. That is two steps, so 2 works.

Structure 3 is $\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{CHO}$. Hydrolyse to $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CHO}$, then strong oxidation with acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ oxidises the secondary alcohol to ketone and the aldehyde to acid at the same time. That is also two steps, so 3 works.

**Test structure 1**

Structure 1 is $\text{CH}_2\text{=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, but-3-en-1-ol. Hydrate the alkene by electrophilic addition of water to give $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, butane-1,3-diol.

Then strong oxidation converts the primary alcohol to $\text{COOH}$ and the secondary alcohol to $\text{C=O}$ in one pot to give $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{COOH}$. That is also two steps, so 1 works.

Since 1, 2 and 3 all work, the correct combination is 1, 2 and 3.

options.A: Correct. All three can give the target in two steps. 1 via hydration then oxidation, 2 via hydrolysis then oxidation, 3 via hydrolysis then double oxidation. Each route passes through a hydroxy intermediate that oxidises to the keto-acid.
options.B: Incorrect. This option omits one valid starting material. Structure 3 is valid because $\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{CHO}$ can be hydrolysed to the hydroxy-aldehyde and then both groups oxidised together with acidified dichromate.
options.C: Incorrect. This option omits structure 1. Students often miss that an alkene can be hydrated to a secondary alcohol, giving butane-1,3-diol which oxidises directly to 3-oxobutanoic acid.
options.D: Incorrect. This option suggests only one structure works. In fact all three contain a functional group (alkene, C-Cl with acid, C-Br with aldehyde) that can be converted to alcohol or diol in step 1 and then oxidised to the required ketone and acid in step 2.
